items.title: New launcher for viral AI mash-ups of Elden Ring, Minecraft, and more emerges – with some very questionable terms of service, should you value your PC
items.content:

(Image credit: FromSoftware) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Those viral Elden Ring and Minecraft mashups you've likely seen circulating the web over the past couple of weeks are now conveniently available to play via a questionably created launcher – one that might compromise your PC in the process.

You know the ones I'm talking about – the AI-powered crossovers boasting the world of Skyrim with the combat of FromSoftware games or whatever – they're everywhere right now. And, as if that wasn't enough, somebody's gone and made (or perhaps vibe coded, as would certainly make sense) a special launcher for Windows computers that supposedly lets you play whatever weird mashup you'd like: Melty.

As per its official description, "Melty is a free mashup launcher for Windows that joins two games you own into one hybrid experience. Instead of installing mods by hand, you press Play once: Melty downloads the mashup, sets up everything the combination needs, and launches the merged game." There's a reason I'm not linking to it here, however. Its terms of service are, uh… Well, they let the launcher do just about everything. They authorize the ability to find games, download new tools, copy files, modify folders, run programs, and execute automatic updates – but that's not all.

I pulled apart the Melty installer (v1.0.33). Under the hood it's a rebrand of LookLoot, an app that records gameplay video + inputs as AI training data. That whole recording system ships inside Melty, and their privacy policy doesn't mention it. A thread🧵 October 5, 2026

A coder who goes by "Wubbity" online alleges that he's "pulled apart" the Melty installer and found that it's "a rebrand of LookLoot, an app that records gameplay video and inputs as AI training data." As he writes, Melty's privacy policy "doesn't mention it."

Although he clarifies it's "not malware, no password stealing," it's "shipping a dormant gameplay-recording pipeline its website can trigger, and users weren't told." In other words, I'd recommend giving this one a miss. That and the Bloodborne PC port similarly relying on AI, and everything else that relies on the controversial tech as it's popping up left, right, and center, it seems. I mean, seriously… it's everywhere.

Valve beats Epic to the punch, updates Steam launcher 1 day before its rival claims to be "faster" "The Robloxification of Steam": Creator of viral game apologizes after rip-offs flood Valve's store Ex-Valve dev not impressed by Epic's updated Steam rival or Tim Sweeney's latest dig at Gabe Newell It doesn't help that reputable (I know, I know) companies like Epic Games are transforming their own launchers and proudly announcing they've "vibe coded" them – although I suppose we still have Valve's ever-legendary Steam to lean on.

If you spot her away from her PC, you'll always find Anna with a fantasy book, a handheld video game console of some sort, and a Tamagotchi or two on hand.

items.title: Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between Manga Matches Road to the Erdtree’s Tone
items.summary: The Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between manga follows Roderika, Brother Corhyn, Rya, and Blackguard Big Boggart.
items.content:
Given the serious nature of the Elden Ring game, it’s honestly pretty amazing that there’s not just one gag manga based on it, but now two comedies building on its established characters and lore. But here we are! Yen Press previously released single chapters of Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between from Haruichi in English, and now the first full volume is out and explores moments in the lives of Roderika, Brother Corhyn, Rya, and Blackguard Big Boggart. It’s less joke-after-joke than Elden Ring: The Road to the Erdtree , while still offering a similar sort of tone.

While the Elden Ring: Road to the Erdtree manga follows a specific Tarnished named Aseo, the Distant Tales Between dedicates each chapter to a major NPC we may or may not meet as we play. It reads more as a short story collection. Which is beneficial, in its way. I think it might be more appealing to someone coming from the game as a result of the decision, since it could be highlighting someone you connected with when playing through your Tarnished’s story. And, at the same time, it’s less focused on constant jokes than the other series Yen Press is handling.

I did find this means some of the individual chapters might feel a little stronger than others. The introduction with Roderika is a perfect point. It is set in essentially a route where a player didn’t encounter her at Stormhill Shack and instead probably already met her after she got to Roundtable Hold. As such, we’re seeing how she reacted and got comfortable there, as well as the response of the other NPCs to her and her situation. Said reactions from other characters are where the comedy comes in, but I also appreciate how it still maintained moments that highlighted the nature of her situation and showed her personal growth.

The more outright comedic tale here is clearly designed to be Blackguard Big Boggart. I promised no spoilers earlier and I meant it, but the best way to describe it is a culinary tour of The Lands Between after he gets fed up with eating prawns. It’s very silly and provides an excuse for him to meet and interact with other established NPCs from our Tarnished’s journey. Plus, I appreciated how each “meal” ended up feeling like both something maybe, vaguely appealing and that would probably be at home in Delicious in Dungeon.

While it does break from the whole “gag” thing the rest of the first volume of the Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between manga has going, I think my favorite chapter here is “The World of Animals: The Springhare’s Excursion.” It’s a wordless look into the life of essentially an ordinary baby bunny in The Lands Between. Which, naturally, means it can get a little harrowing. But it’s also heartwarming at times! And even though there are some concerning moments, it also has a “lighter” sort of feel than someone would expect from Elden Ring and keeps up the tone in that fashion.

The Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between offers the same lighter approach to a manga based on the game as the earlier Road to the Erdtree while also highlighting more characters. Each NPC gets a moment to themselves. While these can be sillier moments, there is still a lot of folks staying somewhat in character, and the stories being told are definitely rooted in established lore to make it more fun.

Volume 1 of the Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between manga is available now, and Yen Press hasn’t shared a release date for the second one yet.

items.title: Before Dark Souls, FromSoftware’s forgotten PS1 horror game was a haunting exercise in empathy
items.summary: Aboard a long-lost ghost ship, this underappreciated game finds tragedy in the stories left untold
items.content:
By Ryan Epps Published Oct 18, 2026, 6:00 AM EDT Ryan Epps is a contributing writer for Polygon. His writing spans both the entertainment and tech verticals, with bylines covering everything from Dark Souls to TVs at sites like Tom’s Guide, IGN, Digital Trends, TheGamer, Tech Times, and more. Halloween Countdown Aboard a long-lost ghost ship, this underappreciated game finds tragedy in the stories left untold

Image: FromSoftware Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google Discover Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap This article is part of a directory: The 2026 Halloween Countdown: 31 days of horror to watch and play Next Before Backrooms, the final season of this horror anthology did creepypasta right To trace FromSoftware’s history is to uncover a lineage written in cold sweat. While the studio is celebrated today for unforgiving action RPGs like Dark Souls and Elden Ring , its DNA is deeply rooted in games that feel born of a fever dream. FromSoft’s darker legacy lives in games like Kuon , a masterclass in Japanese folklore and survival horror, and Shadow Tower , a claustrophobic dungeon crawler that turns every dark alcove into a deadly trap. Even Eternal Ring — not to be confused with its blockbuster sibling Elden Ring — radiates that signature, unsettling aura that makes exploring FromSoftware’s later worlds so intoxicating.

Yet, nearly three decades since its debut, one of the developer’s most compelling experiments in terror remains criminally overlooked. Released in 1998 for the original PlayStation, Echo Night was a radical departure for its era. Uninterested in spilt blood or slaughtered gods, the haunting ghost story traded violence for the melancholic task of laying restless souls to rest on an abandoned cruise ship. Players step into the shoes of Richard Osmond, whose search for his missing father leads to an enigmatic painting that transports him onto the Orpheus, a long-lost ocean liner haunted by spirits trapped in their tragic regrets. To escape, Richard must unravel the ship’s dark history and grant its forgotten passengers the closure they so desperately crave.

Written and produced by Toshifumi Nabeshima, Echo Night rejects the combat-heavy and gory framework of typical ‘90s survival horror in favor of something far more intimate. Rather than leaning into the resource scarcity popularized by Resident Evil , Nabeshima crafted a deeply empathetic adventure built around observation and emotional catharsis. In Echo Night , encounters with hostile spirits don't ask you to pull a trigger, but to frantically race through pitch-black rooms in search of a light switch, as illumination is your only defense against their malice. From there, Nabeshima turns game progression into a series of spectral mercy missions. You might track down a missing ring for a grieving widow or solve a riddle to help a trapped sailor move on, receiving an Astral Piece each time a soul fades into eternal rest. In doing so, Echo Night flips the script on the entire genre: the ghosts aren't obstacles to be destroyed, but victims waiting to be understood.

Image: FromSoftware Although there is an overarching mystery involving Richard’s father and the Orpheus, the game’s true power lies in these more modular tragedies. The Orpheus becomes this vessel of lost lives waiting to be remembered, with one of its most poignant vignettes involving John Cutter. A young crewman trapped in eternal limbo, Cutter endlessly awaits his fiancée, Sistina, who never arrives. He died thinking she had abandoned him, unaware that she had arrived too late and was searching for him in another part of the ship. By delivering a simple keepsake to clear up decades of misunderstanding, Richard resolves a tragic heartbreak, allowing two lingering spirits to finally find each other and peace in the afterlife. It’s in these intimate detours where Echo Night reveals the smaller stories can often have an even more profound impact than the overarching narrative ever could.

Image: FromSoftware The unique formula of Echo Night was compelling enough to spawn a trilogy, though one that remains largely obscure outside of niche horror circles. The Japan-exclusive Echo Night 2: Lord of Nightmares ( Nemuri no Shihaisha ), released in 1999, moved the ghostly investigation to a gothic mansion and refined Nabeshima’s focus on interconnected character vignettes. To this day, series enthusiasts widely consider it the high point of the franchise and well worth seeking out through fan-translation patches. In 2004, the series jumped to the sixth console generation with Echo Night: Beyond , transporting players to an abandoned research base on the Moon. Though critics at the time balked at its slow pace and polarizing suit-oxygen mechanics, Beyond has since earned a devoted cult following. It never lost sight of the series’ core identity of a melancholic journey where helping lost souls find closure is your only true objective.

A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Echo Night puts forth a sensibility that feels quietly prevalent in FromSoftware’s later work. The mournful environmental storytelling of Dark Souls and the fragmented lore of Elden Ring share this exact DNA, insisting players actively piece together forgotten tragedies themselves rather than having them passively explained through dialogue or long, drawn-out cutscenes. As such, Echo Night stands as a fascinating proto-Soulslike in spirit if not in combat, a game where compassion takes precedence over violence, and where the ultimate victory isn't slaying a god, but helping a forsaken soul finally rest.

Image: FromSoftware In an industry that so often turns death into a sport and horror into a shooting gallery, Echo Night stands as a quiet act of resistance. Even after all this time, it reminds us that horror can be far more devastating when it’s not born from a monster in the dark, but from the tragedy of being forgotten. Long before FromSoftware taught us how to survive their grueling nightmares, Echo Night showed us how to heal them, leaving behind a poignant ghost story that doesn't haunt the player with fear but lingers in the heart like a half-remembered lullaby.

items.title: Why Do Big Games Keep Being Made Playable In Browsers? A Guide To Vibe-Coded Ports
PlayStation Plus' new Elden Ring rival tackles my biggest issue with FromSoftware's work
items.summary: Variety is the spice of life, they say ✨
items.content:
The PlayStation Plus October bumper drop adds a soulsgame I'd highly recommend to those who find FromSoftware's work a bit too tedious.

PlayStation Plus’ October bumper drop includes some excellent games for your PlayStation Plus Extra subscription, but it's the Premium offering that’s caught our eye.

To be more specific PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers get access to one of my new favourite soulslikes, one I’d even hold above some FromSoftware titles.

That may sound like sacrilege to some, but hear me out. Since my early teen years I’ve been a massive fan of FromSoftware, with Dark Souls being one of my favourite games ever made. In fact it’s my Game of the Year, every year .

However, Mortal Shell II seriously impressed me, so I’m thrilled that more people get to experience it through PlayStation Plus Premium. On October 20 a free trial will launch.

It’s tough to make a soulslike game feel like anything but a half-hearted attempt to ride FromSoftware’s coattails, though many games like Lies of P have done a good job of being unique.

Mortal Shell II joins that exclusive club with its core mechanic, ‘shells’. Rather than creating one character and slowly creating a build as time goes on, Mortal Shell II gives you flexibility. The shells are found throughout the world and each one has its own stats, weapons and more.

You can freely switch between them, which tackles one of the few gripes I have with FromSoftware games. When I play soulslikes I often find myself naturally gravitating towards a strength-build. It’s the “big stick go bonk” caveman approach a lot of players find themselves slipping into and while it is good fun, by the end of my playthrough I wish I’d done things differently.

Elden Ring thankfully breaks tradition and lets you change your build with Larval Tears, though there’s a finite supply so you can’t get too crazy with it. It also doesn’t solve another problem; weapons. To fully change your build in Elden Ring you need to alter your stats, find an upgrade new weapons to compliment your build, and of course acquire new drip to match your new personality.

Mortal Shell II trims the fat, and while it doesn’t make the game easier by any means it does make it more engaging.

After recently going hands-on with Phantom Blade Zero I was thoroughly impressed with the way it’s handling its weapon upgrades, and the same theory is being applied in Mortal Shell II; players need variety.

READ NEXT: 6 reasons why Phantom Blade Zero will be the best action game of all-time

FromSoftware’s unlikely to adopt this style of gameplay in its future games and to be honest I hope it doesn’t, but it is something other soulslikes should take note of.

We shouldn’t need to start entirely new playthroughs just to try something new. It should be baked into the gameplay in one way or another.

items.title: Which sci-fi film will bring Zendaya and Alex Garland together?
items.summary: Screenwriter and director Alex Garland, at the helm of the film adaptation of Elden Ring, is preparing a new sci-fi project starring Zendaya.
items.content:
British screenwriter and director Alex Garland ( Ex Machina , Civil War ) is at the helm of the film adaptation of Elden Ring , the video game co-created by George R.R. Martin, the mastermind behind the Game of Thrones saga. In 2027, he will then turn his attention to a sci-fi project starring Zendaya.

It has been A24 ’s boldest gamble so far. The American independent studio known for Everything Everywhere All at Once (2022), Civil War (2024) and Marty Supreme (2026) is investing more than $100 million in the adaptation of Elden Ring . This dark fantasy video game was developed by FromSoftware ( Dark Souls ) under the direction of Hidetaka Miyazaki and based on the mythology imagined by George R.R. Martin , author of the cult literary saga Game of Throne s. A24’s previous budget record was held by Marty Supreme (2026), starring Timothée Chalamet , with $70 million.

Released in 2022, the game has sold more than 30 million copies and won over 400 Game of the Year awards. In a world known as the Lands Between, the Elden Ring, the source of all order, has been shattered by the descendants of Queen Marika, corrupted demigods who divided its fragments among themselves and plunged the kingdom into chaos. Players take on the role of a Tarnished, an exile summoned back to journey across this ravaged land, confront the demigods and restore the Ring in order to become the new Elden Lord…

Cailee Spaeny for the Los Angeles premiere Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery , at the Academy of Motion Pictures on November 17th, 2025. © JC Olivera/Variety via Getty Images. Cailee Spaeny, star of Alex Garland’s new feature The adaptation was only made possible thanks to Alex Garland’s determination. The British filmmaker behind Ex Machina (2014), Annihilation (2018) and Civil War (2024) wrote a 160-page screenplay accompanied by 40 pages of visuals, before travelling to Japan to pitch the project directly to Hidetaka Miyazaki , who gave him his blessing.

As for the cast, Kit Connor , who rose to fame in the series Heartstopper and worked with Alex Garland in Warfare (2025), will take on the lead role. He will be joined by Ben Whishaw ( Black Doves ) and Cailee Spaeny ( Priscilla , Alien: Romulus ), who previously worked with Alex Garland on Civil War . Alongside them are Tom Burke ( Furiosa ), Nick Offerman ( The Last of Us ), Havana Rose Liu ( Bottoms ), Sonoya Mizuno ( Ex Machina ) and Jonathan Pryce ( The Crown ).

Zendaya at the Louis Vuitton Spring/Summer 2027 show in Paris. © Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images pour Louis Vuitton. A sci-fi film starring Zendaya The filming of Elden Ring started in April 2026 in the United Kingdom, particularly in Scotland, with additional sequences shot in Iceland last summer. Two ideal locations for bringing the game’s medieval dark fantasy universe to the screen, with its colossal Gothic architecture and Lovecraftian creatures lurking in bleak, terrifying landscapes.

But Alex Garland is already setting another project in motion, this time starring Zendaya . It will be a sci-fi film produced by A24. While filming is scheduled for 2027, the feature has no official title or synopsis yet. The project will allow the actress to return to a genre (science fiction) she knows well thanks to the Dune saga.

Elden Ring (2028) by Alex Garland does not have a release date yet. Alex Garland’s sci-fi film starring Zendaya does not have a title or release date yet.

items.title: The 6 Best Video Games Released Since 2020, Ranked
items.summary: From Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 to Elden Ring, these six flawless modern video games skip the checklists for absolute obsession.
items.content:
Astarion in Baldur's Gate 3 Image via Larian Studios By Safwan Azeem Published Oct 15, 2026, 1:08 PM EDT Feel free to connect with him or check out his work. He's everywhere — Upwork , YouTube , Spotify , SoundCloud , Collider , LinkedIn , Instagram .

on Google Preferred Source Google Discover Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap There are games you finish , and there are games that temporarily reorganize your life. You start thinking about builds while brushing your teeth. You hear a soundtrack cue in your head when nobody is playing anything. You swear you are only checking one side path and somehow it is 2:17 a.m. and you have accidentally discovered an underground civilization, adopted three strangers, betrayed a god, or spent forty minutes trying to launch a wooden cart off a mountain because the physics looked funny.

That is the level we are dealing with here. These games do not merely contain great combat or good stories. They create obsession through completely different means. These are my 6 favorite video games released since 2020 .

Image via Sandfall Interactive Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 begins in Lumière, where an entity known as the Paintress wakes once a year and paints a number on a distant monolith. Everyone of that age immediately disappears. When she paints “33,” Gustave and the latest expedition cross the sea with one purpose: reach her and somehow stop the cycle before another generation is erased.

That premise already has teeth, but what floored me was how beautiful the game is willing to be while talking constantly about death. Sandfall Interactive built Belle Époque elegance into something dreamlike and rotten, full of impossible landscapes, broken architecture, and characters who know their own clocks are running out. Then the combat starts asking you to stay physically engaged instead of hiding behind menu choices. Parries, dodges, timed attacks — suddenly a turn-based battle has your entire body leaning toward the screen . And the story keeps taking emotional swings I genuinely did not expect. This is one of those games where saying too much is vandalism. Go in knowing the expedition is doomed enough to understand the urgency. Let the rest hit you properly.

A giant robot crushing things in Astro Bot Image via Team ASOBI I had forgotten how good it feels when a game simply wants you to smile. Astro Bot sends the tiny robot hero across a galaxy of compact platforming worlds after his PS5-shaped mothership is wrecked, scattering his crew and vital ship parts across dozens of planets. Team Asobi takes that excuse and turns it into a toy box. One level gives Astro giant punching gloves. Another shrinks him. Another lets him absorb water until he becomes an adorable walking balloon.

The references to PlayStation history are wonderful, but nostalgia is almost the least interesting thing about it. The reason this game landed so hard is movement. Astro’s feet patter differently across metal and glass. Sand shifts. Controllers vibrate. Tiny robots cheer when you rescue them. A hidden platform can make you laugh before you even land on it. There is no insecurity here about being colorful or cute or straightforwardly fun. In an era where every major release sometimes feels pressured to become a hundred-hour lifestyle, Astro Bot strolls in, hands you a penguin power-up, and reminds you that delight is still a serious design achievement.

Melinöe holding a scythe in Hades 2 Image via Supergiant Games Melinoë has a wonderfully horrible family problem. In Hades II , the immortal witch-princess trains in the Crossroads to defeat Chronos, the Titan of Time, after he seizes the House of Hades and imprisons much of her family. Supergiant Games takes the foundation of the original Hades and shifts the entire emotional temperature. Zagreus was trying to escape home. Melinoë is trying to reclaim one.

You feel that difference everywhere. Her combat is more ritualistic, more deliberate, full of witchcraft, cast circles, Ω attacks, familiars, incantations, and boons from gods who somehow remain extremely attractive while discussing divine warfare. But the secret weapon is still failure. You lose a run and come home richer in conversation. Hecate comments on your progress. Nemesis gets under your skin. Odysseus has advice. Moros appears with that wonderfully doomed energy. Then you go out again because maybe this combination of Apollo, Aphrodite, and Hestia will turn you into an unstoppable catastrophe. Supergiant somehow understands that a roguelike becomes addictive when dying feels less like losing progress and more like returning to people you wanted to see anyway.

Image via Nintendo The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom starts with Link and Zelda exploring beneath Hyrule Castle, where they awaken an ancient evil connected to Ganondorf. Zelda disappears, Link loses much of his strength, the Master Sword is shattered, and enormous islands suddenly hang in the sky above a Hyrule that now has an entire nightmare world hidden underneath it. And Nintendo’s response to all of that is basically: here, glue this wheel to a plank and see what happens.

That should not work. It works magnificently. Ultrahand lets you attach objects together, which means the game stops treating environmental puzzles as questions with one respectable answer. Need to cross a ravine? Build a bridge. Build a car. Build a terrible aircraft that flips over immediately. Strap twelve fans to a sled and become an enemy of engineering. Fuse turns random junk into weapons. Recall lets you reverse an object’s movement. Ascend makes ceilings feel suspicious because suddenly every roof might be a doorway. I love Tears of the Kingdom because Nintendo gives you godlike tools and then tolerates your stupidity with extraordinary patience. Half the adventure is saving Hyrule. The other half is discovering whether a machine powered by six rockets can launch a Korok into low orbit.

Elden Ring Image via FromSoftware The first person in Elden Ring who tells you your destiny also insults you. You are Tarnished. You have returned to the Lands Between after the shattering of the Elden Ring, and eventually you are supposed to gather Great Runes and become Elden Lord. That sounds like a standard heroic mission until FromSoftware actually lets you loose and you realize practically every beautiful object on the horizon has something underneath it capable of killing you in two hits. Nothing prepared me for walking out into Limgrave the first time. There is the Erdtree dominating the sky, ruined churches in the distance, a mounted knight patrolling five minutes from your starting point, and absolutely nobody explaining which direction is “correct.” So you wander.

That generosity is what makes it extraordinary. Miyazaki and the team at FromSoftware did not make discovery a checklist reward. They made discovery feel slightly illegal. You constantly stumble into things that seem too significant to have been hidden where you found them. Malenia can become an optional obsession. Ranni’s quest can consume an entire evening of reading item descriptions and texting friends, “Where the hell is Blaidd?” Elden Ring trusts curiosity more than instructions, and once a game gives you that feeling, normal open worlds start looking suspiciously organized.

A screenshot from 'Baldur's Gate 3'. Image via Larian Studios My favorite thing about Baldur's Gate 3 is that it is completely willing to let you be an idiot and then honor the consequences. The game opens with your character infected by a mind flayer parasite that should eventually transform you into one of the creatures responsible. You escape the nautiloid carrying that problem into the Forgotten Realms, meet other infected survivors, and start looking for a cure while the situation grows into something vastly larger involving the Absolute, ancient powers, rival factions, and a collection of companions whose personal disasters could each support their own RPG. That explanation barely captures what playing it feels like.

items.title: Opinion: Elden Ring Is One Of My Favourite Games That I've Hardly Played
items.content:
I have started a new Elden Ring save file on four separate occasions now, and I have absolutely adored my time with each of them. And yet, despite putting 15-20 hours minimum into each new load, my current Switch 2 playthrough is the first time that I've managed to push through the 'tutorial area'.

I need to do some explaining here, because if you have never ventured into the Lands Between, then three save files and 60+ hours spent in a tutorial sounds insane. However, in the grand scheme of things, it's not that bad .

After pushing you through a very brief 'real' tutorial — one that introduces you to the basics of Elden Ring's combat and movement — your Tarnished avatar is funnelled into Limgrave and beckoned towards Stormveil Castle as your first major objective. However, rushing straight to the battlements will put you up against foes and challenges that you are severely underprepared for, so the game encourages you to instead take a stroll around the area and perhaps venture down to the locales south of it in the Weeping Peninsula.

Much like Breath of the Wild 's Great Plateau, this is the game's actual tutorial. But I cannot stress this enough, it makes Link's wakeup spot look tiny.

Limgrave and its surrounding areas are huge and so densely packed with things to do that one could happily play this zone as a game of its own. Heck, for my first three save files, that's exactly what I did.

I explored the nooks and crannies of all the region's catacombs, took on mini bosses and Minor Erdtrees, solved environmental puzzles to unlock new gear, and took on sidequests that involved storylines and platforming challenges of their own.

On my first save back in 2022, by the time that I finally pushed through the game's first 'roadblock' boss, Margit (yes, there is a way around him, but I didn't see that at the time), I was quite content with the 20-odd hours I had put into Elden Ring, and I went off to play something else. Save files two and three saw me go further still, through the game's first real dungeon and into the boss on the other side. On both these occasions, I polished off Godrick the Grafted (a proper FromSoft name, if I've ever heard one) with relative ease, but was deterred by what awaited me afterwards: the proper game .

Just like the first time that you paraglide off the Great Plateau and realise everything you've explored up to this point is just a tiny proportion of what the whole map has to offer, stepping into Lunaria of the Lakes is a similarly daunting task. The zone's entry point even has a vantage point vaguely reminiscent of leaving the Shrine of Resurrection, for crying out loud.

For save files two and three, the scope of what was to come was simply too much. I had had a wonderful time with everything I had played up until that point, and loved how it all culminated in a challenging dungeon and gruesome boss. Honestly, I couldn't bring myself to do it all over again.

Until the Tarnished Edition arrived on Switch 2, that is. I finally got around to starting save file number four a few weeks back, and believe me when I say, I have not been able to put it down.

I did my usual Limgrave exploration, ventured into the fiery Caelid region (and swiftly realised I was still far too weak for it), and steadily levelled up in various catacombs and hoard encounters. Unsurprisingly, I dispatched both Margit and Godrick in one or two attempts — I've played 'em both more than enough by now — and Stormveil was similarly breezy for someone who's spent so much time in it over the years. But then something unexpected happened: I kept playing.

Despite my previous cowardice, I stepped boldly into the uncharted waters of 'The Lakes' and I still haven't quit. As I am writing this, I have just polished off The Academy of Raya Lucaria (a dungeon that, as someone using a magic build, can get in the bin) and its Good Boi / Bad Gurl bosses, and I still want more.

Aside from the portability perk — I couldn't put this version down, even if I wanted to — the Switch 2 port itself is absolutely sublime. All those months of convention footage and delays had me worried that I'd never be able to play a game this reliant on reaction times with a choppy frame rate, but it all holds up remarkably well. Performance certainly hasn't been perfect, and I have encountered some substantial drops here and there, but I'm finding myself enjoying this version even more than my prior attempts on PS4 and PS5 (and I loved those attempts).

Having spoken to some friends that are absolutely head-over-heels for this game, I know that I am very much still in the early stages of what Elden Ring has to offer, and there's every chance that I'll butt up against another roadblock down the line and bring save file four to an end.

He built his might out of love and loyalty, an unstoppable force that bade the stars to halt at the cry of a true champion. His golden armor, his raging snarl, even the gravity crests on his blades can be made out with perfect clarity. items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before playing.

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

    [/*]

  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.

    [/*]

  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent: - Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle. - Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes. - Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau. Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.

    [/*]

  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital. Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching 28th August on Nintendo Switch 2
What Is Elden Ring About?
items.summary: Discover what Elden Ring is about: a dark fantasy epic by FromSoftware & George R.R. Martin, set in a vast open world. Join 30M+ players and become the next Elden Lord!
items.content:
The legend of ELDEN RING is a dark fantasy epic born from a collaboration between two masters of the genre.

Using the seed of a story about bloodline, heritage and betrayal written by George R.R. Martin , Hidetaka Miyazaki and FromSoftware have crafted a vast and beautiful wilderness out of the ruins of a kingdom fractured by war between demigods.

After the assassination of Godwyn the Golden , her oldest son, god queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring that was the source of her power. Her remaining children took up these pieces for themselves. Using the might these runes gave them, the Demigods fought to become her successor, each driven by their own motives.

However, this maddening war was a stalemate with no clear victor. The Demigods retreated to their respective realms as the world fell further and further into stagnation, the Golden Order sundered.

But now, a group of banished warriors known as the Tarnished are returning to the Lands Between . You are one of those Tarnished , the dead who yet live, drawn by the guidance of what grace remains to seek the throne and become the next Elden Lord .

Read more about the story of ELDEN RING’s Age of the Gods, the history crafted by George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki.

The world of ELDEN RING is dangerous and majestic. Pale grasslands lead to flooded plains where dragons roost. A crimson battlefield now seethes under scarlet swamps of rot. You’ll climb frozen mountains, search through mystical forests, conquer golden kingdoms, and that’s only the beginning.

All of these rich landscapes are host to deadly enemies and wonderous secrets. There are caves and deep crypts guarded by traps, forts that have fallen to rebellions, and ruins of past civilizations that are now home to monsters and madmen.

Most intricate of all are the vast legacy dungeons like Stormveil castle , whose ramparts crown the high hills of Limgrave . Many of these sprawling dungeons host the remaining Demigods who guard their Great Runes within.

As you travel, you may also find the few souls who remain in the land still possessed of their wits and intellect. Most still retain their ambitions as well and may ask for your help. Aid or hinder them as you see fit, either way could benefit you in some manner if you are wise.

Prepare to explore the Lands Between with our ELDEN RING Starter Guide.

For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games. The broader gaming culture has defined titles that take their inspiration from the Souls series as being part of a “Soulslike” genre .

The Souls series has many unique features, but the genre is defined by three main features. All Souls series games have combat focused on precise timing and evasion that is simple to learn but challenging to master.

They also include a system that requires the player to survive between checkpoints at the risk of losing the currency they receive from defeating enemies that is used to purchase stat upgrades. And of course, the Souls series feature intense, memorable boss fights that test the player’s skills to progress through the story.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
